chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hajjaj, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the blind man: is his testimony accepted? He said, 'Yes, if he is established (i.e., not a recent convert or doubtful in his vision/condition).'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a blind person accepted in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that blindness does not inherently invalidate testimony, provided the witness is 'established' (ithbat). In Shia jurisprudence, this condition typically refers to the witness being a known, reliable believer (thiqah) whose character and faith are well-documented, ensuring their testimony carries weight despite the lack of visual verification.
